cw: The Shanghai outpost of Taiwan-based Classic Works brings its eye for substantial boots and independent shoemaking to Xinzha Road. The selection spans Viberg, Wesco, Rolling Dub Trio, Heschung, Ruttshoes and Katsuya Tokunaga. Give yourself time to handle the leather, compare construction and try contrasting lasts across American, European and Japanese makers.
rb: Special collaborations and well-made, fashion-forward footwear are the draw at Radiance Blue. Its selection brings American classics into conversation with contemporary and outdoor design, with names including Alden, G.H. Bass, Vinny’s and Scarpa. Visit to compare distinctive collaborations, materials and silhouettes on the third floor of HKRI Taikoo Hui.
jl: John Lobb’s Plaza 66 boutique, now on level B1, is a focused destination for ready-to-wear shoemaking. Compare last shapes, leather and finishing, and explore how different models fit your feet. The boutique also offers a full range of shoe-care and recrafting services for John Lobb footwear, making it a destination for existing owners as well as new buyers.
rl: Ralph Lauren’s footwear merits attention for its connections with established international shoemakers. RRL brings workwear and heritage boots, including English- and American-made examples. The collector reports that most recent Purple Label shoes he has seen are Italian-made; this is a personal observation, not a verified share of production. Shoe origin varies by model and period. Compare the leather, construction and fit of the available pairs, then continue to nearby NOOS.
rl2: A Bund-side stop to explore Purple Label shoes: their proportions, leather and finishing. The collector reports that most recent Purple Label shoes he has seen are Italian-made; this is a personal observation, not a verified share of production. Shoe origin varies by model and period. Ask which footwear models and sizes the Peninsula boutique currently carries before making a dedicated trip.
rr: Heritage clothing and specialist footwear meet at The Real Real Co., with names including Clinch, Role Club, Brother Bridge and Sanders. For boot enthusiasts, the attraction is the chance to compare distinctive shapes and makers rarely encountered together. Find the shop at 33 Shaanxi South Road.
bj: A lane-house destination for British and European shoemaking, with Tricker’s, Cheaney, Carmina and Gaziano & Girling in its selection. BaronJ is particularly worth visiting for Gaziano & Girling made-to-order commissions, with time to discuss the choices behind a personal pair. Arrange access for this weekend and appointment-based stop.
fy: A stop for Shanghai’s everyday canvas-shoe tradition, with Feiyue at its center. Culture Matters also offers custom Feiyue painting and personalization through its in-house artist team, turning a familiar canvas shoe into an individual piece. Explore the designs at the Wulumuqi Middle Road shop and connect the visit with the atlas’s Feiyue history entry.
ic: A select shop whose footwear crosses several distinct traditions: J.M. Weston, Alden, Hender Scheme and Guidi. That mix makes it a compelling place to explore the distance between classic leather shoes and more experimental treatments of familiar forms. Allow time to compare silhouettes, leather and fit.
pn: An opportunity to explore a Shanghai footwear label on its own terms. Visit the flagship to see how PANE approaches sneaker proportions, material combinations and everyday wear. Try different silhouettes: the relationship between shape, weight and fit is the useful part of seeing the collection in person.
ro: A concentrated stop for English, Italian and Chinese shoemaking, with names including George Cleverley, Edward Green, Stefano Bemer, Enzo Bonafè, Antonio Meccariello and Oct Tenth. Compare makers’ approaches to shape and finishing, with particular interest in Chinese hand-welted work. Roiluxe frequently hosts Chinese maker trunk shows, bringing collectors into direct conversation with the people making their shoes.
lm: A shoe salon within La Maison, where footwear can be considered alongside tailoring. The selection combines The Anthology’s collaborations with shoes curated with Tassels Hong Kong, including names such as Crockett & Jones, Bowhill & Elliott and Alden. The setting lends itself to considering proportions and how a pair works with trousers and a complete outfit.
rv: A broad footwear stop within Xintiandi Dongtai Li, bringing together artisanal leather shoes, boots and heritage clothing. Makers include Buttero, Lemargo, Shoto and Danner, offering several approaches to texture, silhouette and everyday wear. Take time to handle the leather and compare the individual shoes on the second floor of Building D.
md: A reason for footwear enthusiasts to cross to Pudong. MEDALLION’s offering spans ready-to-wear, made-to-order and bespoke, with makers including Saint Crispin’s, Gaziano & Girling, Paolo Scafora, TLB Mallorca and ACME. Allow time to discuss fit and the differences between buying an available pair and commissioning one.
gm: A destination for shoe care, repair and restoration, with a connection to shoemaker Zhou Ruoda and his two brands: San Pomodoro, offering women’s custom Goodyear-welted shoes, and Songs of Love and Hate, his bespoke shoemaking brand. The stop connects the upkeep of well-loved footwear with contemporary Chinese making and the possibilities of a personal commission.
no: Edward Green and Crockett & Jones anchor this compact English-shoemaking stop. Compare lasts, leather and finishing across the two makers, and explore made-to-order possibilities. Pair it with Ralph Lauren elsewhere in Kerry Centre for a broader look at classic footwear. NOOS is in the South Building; Ralph Lauren is in the North Building.
no2: The Xujiahui branch brings NOOS’s Edward Green and Crockett & Jones selection to the southern part of the circuit. Explore the two English makers through their shapes, leather and fit, or combine the visit with an afternoon around Xujiahui. Find the boutique at L235-2 in One ITC.
fs: A heritage-clothing and vintage stop in Hongkou’s Music Valley, with coffee adding a reason to linger. The clothing offers context for the heritage shoes and boots found elsewhere on the circuit. Treat it as an optional neighborhood detour, with time to browse the clothing and explore the surrounding streets.
eth: A destination for exploring avant-garde footwear in person, with a core of GUIDI, m.a+, A1923 and limited-edition Geoffrey B. Small shoes. A large visvim selection adds a distinctive Japanese perspective alongside those European makers. The attraction is the opportunity to examine leather, construction and unconventional proportions at close range. Allow time for fitting: distinctive shapes can feel and look quite different on the foot than in photographs.
doet: A Shanghai streetwear stop for sports shoes, special releases and collaborations. Explore contemporary sneaker design through color, materials and the details that distinguish a collaborative edition. The Tongren Road shop adds a different perspective to a Jing’an circuit of traditional shoemaking and specialist boots.
doeh: A sneaker and streetwear stop near Xintiandi, convenient to combine with the central Huangpu circuit. Explore sports shoes, collaborations and special releases alongside the clothing that gives them context. The Hubin Road location is a natural addition to an afternoon around Xintiandi and Dongtai Li.
cmxt: The Xintiandi branch of Culture Matters offers another way into Shanghai’s canvas-shoe culture, with Feiyue at the center. Find it on B1 of Xintiandi Style at 245 Madang Road, then continue north towards DOE on Hubin Road and Rivets at Dongtai Li. Choose this branch or Wulumuqi Middle Road if you want a single Culture Matters visit; ask which styles and sizes are available here.
juice: Edison Chen’s JUICE brings CLOT and sneaker collaborations to a Julu Road house. The Shanghai store opened in 2009 and remains listed in JUICE’s official store directory. Visit for the streetwear side of the circuit, compare the footwear on the floor and ask about current releases. It pairs naturally with nearby Industrial Co.; special editions and sizes change with each release.
autumn: An independent select shop on Taiyuan Road, with an artisanal footwear thread running through its clothing and accessories. Its published brand list includes Cherevichkiotvichki, Muñoz Vrandecic and Paul Harnden Shoemakers. Explore distinctive shapes, worked leathers and the relationship between shoes and clothing; ask which footwear and sizes are currently available. Pair it with La Maison and eth0s on the southern part of the central circuit.
fly: A Shanghai skate shop with roots in 1999 and a history of Nike SB collaborations. The Gardenia Dunk connects sneaker design with the city’s street culture. For a customization visit, ask what shoe personalization, if any, is currently offered; a design collaboration does not establish an in-store service.
nikelab: A temporary sneaker stop to inquire about NikeLab releases and customization. Jing Daily reported that X158 at 158 Xinle Road would close on 7 October 2026, with a pop-up at Yanqingfang, 122 Yanqing Road, from 8 October. Customization services at this location have not been confirmed.
mandom: A key Jiashan Road destination for footwear within a wider selection of independent menswear. Look for Yuketen, Baudoin & Lange and Sanders, and ask about Green George’s Italian shoes and boots. The range brings together heritage footwear and more refined loafers, with clothing from makers such as Anatomica, Big Yank, Wythe, Tenjin Works and Scarti-Lab. Inside High Street Loft, a short continuation south from eth0s, this is a stop to allow time for trying different shapes, leathers and constructions.
gl: A useful Pudong destination for comparing British welted shoes and contemporary Italian footwear. The collector reports seeing Church’s, Cheaney, Loake, Barker, Sanders and Officine Creative in the second-floor shoe selection at Galeries Lafayette, L+Mall. This is a first-hand observation, not an independently verified current inventory. A 2024 industry report documents an ESTATE footwear concession at Shanghai Galeries Lafayette. Compare lasts, leathers and construction in person; confirm the concession, models and sizes before a dedicated trip.
